questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution specifies the composition of the Council of States?
questions.solution:
Article 80 specifies the composition of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
  • Composition: Maximum 250 members, including 12 nominated by the President and up to 238 representatives of States and UTs.

questions.question: Concurrent list of seventh schedule does NOT have provision related to ______.
questions.solution:
Taxes on lands and buildings is a subject under the State List, not the Concurrent List.
  • Concurrent List Items: Includes 'Industrial and labour disputes', 'Forests', and 'Economic and social planning'.

questions.question: State public services; State Public Service Commission comes under which list of seventh schedule of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
State public services and the State Public Service Commission are subjects mentioned in the State List (List II) of the Seventh Schedule.
  • Contrast: UPSC and All India Services fall under the Union List.

questions.question: Central Bureau of Intelligence and Investigation comes under which list of the seventh schedule of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The Central Bureau of Intelligence and Investigation (CBI) falls under the Union List.
  • Logic: Matters of national security, intelligence, and central investigation agencies are strictly under the purview of the Central Government.

questions.question: In which year was a law passed in India to make conversion to Christianity easier?
questions.solution:
The Caste Disabilities Removal Act, 1850 (Lex Loci Act) was passed to make conversion to Christianity easier.
  • Impact: It allowed a person who converted from Hinduism to another religion to inherit their ancestral property, which was previously prohibited.

questions.question: The part VII of the Indian constitution has been omitted. It is related with which of the following?
questions.option_1: Reservation for Anglo –Indian communities in parliament
questions.option_2: Armed forces in states in part A of the second schedule
questions.option_3: States in part B of the first schedule
questions.solution:
Part VII (which dealt with States in Part B of the First Schedule) was omitted by the 7th Amendment Act, 1956.
  • Context: This amendment abolished the classification of states into Parts A, B, C, and D, moving toward the current system of States and Union Territories.

questions.question: Which of the following comes under 5th schedule of the Indian constitution?
questions.option_1: Provisions related to Oaths or Affirmations
questions.option_2: Provisions related to Tribal areas in states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
questions.option_4: Provisions related to Schedule Areas and Scheduled Tribes
questions.solution:
The 5th Schedule deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
  • Difference: The 6th Schedule specifically handles Tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.

questions.question: Which among the following is not required to be the Vice-President of India?
questions.option_1: He should not hold any office of profit under the Union government or any state government or any local authority or any other public authority.
questions.option_2: He should be a citizen of India.
questions.option_3: He should beQualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha.
questions.option_4: He should have completed 40 years of age.
questions.solution:
The requirement to have completed 40 years of age is INCORRECT for the Vice-President.
  • Actual Age: A person must be at least 35 years old to be the Vice-President (same as President and Governor).

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution specifies Hindi as official language of the Union?
questions.solution:
Article 343 declares Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language of the Union.
  • English: It also provided for the continued use of English for official purposes for a period of 15 years (later extended).

questions.question: The Indian parliament has power to impose restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse through which article of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
Article 302 empowers Parliament to impose restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce, or intercourse in the public interest.
  • Limit: These restrictions must not be discriminatory between states unless there is a scarcity of goods.

questions.question: Under which article of the Indian constitution is the Prime Minister the head of the Council of Ministers?
questions.solution:
Article 74 establishes that the Prime Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers.
  • Function: The Council exists to aid and advise the President, who must act according to such advice.

questions.question: When did depressed classes get the reserved seats in provincial and central legislative councils, but they were to be voted in by General electorate?
questions.solution:
The Depressed Classes received reserved seats through the Poona Pact in September 1932.
  • Signatories: Signed between B.R. Ambedkar and M.K. Gandhi (on behalf of upper-caste Hindus) to abandon separate electorates in favor of reserved seats within the General electorate.

questions.question: Article 26 of the Indian constitution is related with which of the following?
questions.option_3: Freedom as to payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion
questions.solution:
Article 26 guarantees the freedom to manage religious affairs.
  • Rights: This includes establishing institutions for religious purposes, managing own affairs in matters of religion, and owning/acquiring property.

questions.question: Who is the highest law officer in India?
questions.solution:
The Attorney General for India (Article 76) is the highest law officer in the country.
  • Rights: He has the right of audience in all courts in India and can participate in Parliamentary proceedings without the right to vote.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution states that “Governor has power to promulgate ordinances during recess of legislature”?
questions.solution:
Article 213 empowers the Governor to promulgate ordinances when the state legislature is not in session.
  • Mirror Article: This is the state-level equivalent of the President's power under Article 123.

questions.question: Article related to compulsory acquisition of property has been omitted now from the Indian constitution. What is the number of this article?
questions.solution:
Article 31 (Compulsory acquisition of property) was omitted by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
  • Legal Status: It is now a legal right under Article 300-A.

questions.question: Which among the following is not a type of Right to freedom in the Indian constitution?
questions.option_1: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
questions.option_2: Protection of life and personal liberty.
questions.option_4: Protection in respect of conviction for offences.
questions.solution:
Offences for armed assembly is NOT a type of Right to Freedom.
  • Right to Freedom (Art 19-22): Includes speech, assembly (peaceful and without arms), life/liberty, and protection against conviction.

questions.question: Which among the following Constitutional Amendment Act of the Indian constitution reduced the age of voting from 21 to 18 for elections to the Lok Sabha and to the Legislative Assemblies of states?
questions.solution:
The 61st Amendment Act, 1988 reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years.
  • Implementation: This was first applied during the 1989 General Elections.

questions.question: Which Constitution Amendment Act added provisions related to Municipalities in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The 74th Amendment Act, 1992 added provisions related to Municipalities (Part IX-A).
  • 73rd Amendment: Added Panchayats (Part IX).

questions.question: Which of the following Constitution Amendment Act made the Right to education a Fundamental Right under article 21 A of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 made the Right to Education (Article 21-A) a Fundamental Right.
  • Target: Free and compulsory education for children between 6 and 14 years.

questions.question: Which amendment in the Indian constitution is related to extension of jurisdiction of High Courts to Union territories?
questions.solution:
The 7th Amendment Act, 1956 empowered Parliament to extend the jurisdiction of a High Court to any Union Territory.
  • Example: The jurisdiction of the Kerala High Court extends to Lakshadweep.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution specifies equality before the law?
questions.solution:
Article 14 specifies Equality before the Law and Equal Protection of the Laws.
  • Concept: It ensures that no person is above the law and that like should be treated as like.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian woman to be appointed Chief Justice of a state High Court?
questions.solution:
Leila Seth became the first Indian woman to be appointed Chief Justice of a state High Court (Himachal Pradesh HC) in 1991.
  • Anna Chandy: First female judge of a High Court.
  • M. Fathima Beevi: First female judge of the Supreme Court.
